Bunrei 分霊 data: how to get authoritative 系統 coverage without the two paper sources

Written 2026-07-07 at Emma's request, replacing the parked 神社本庁 (1995) / 岡田荘司 book route. Everything below is orderable by effort and expected yield; nothing here requires library access.

Where we stand

Total~10,550each edge cited S854; P612 = network head (総本社)

Four research agents already established there is no downloadable branch→head dataset anywhere (government, academic, LOD, commercial, community). The current derivation classifies shrines into networks by ja-label suffix and points P612 at the network head — the immediate kanjō parent is published nowhere as a dataset. The remaining ceiling: shrines whose names don't match their network suffix, small networks, and per-shrine (not per-network) provenance.

The avenues, ranked

1. jawiki 由緒 prose harvest — 勧請元 statements high yieldoffline

Japanese Wikipedia shrine articles routinely state the source shrine in prose: 「石清水八幡宮から勧請」「伏見稲荷大社より分霊を勧請した」 — in the 由緒/歴史 section or the infobox 主祭神/創建 fields. This is the only avenue that yields the immediate kanjō parent rather than the network head — strictly better data than what we have.

  • Method: offline pass over the jawiki dump (we already walk ~6,700 shrine articles for the reisai import — same infrastructure). Regex family: (.{2,20}?(神宮|大社|神社|八幡宮))(から|より)(分霊を)?勧請 plus 分祀/分社/御分霊 variants. Each hit → branch P612 source | S4656 jawiki-URL.
  • Expected yield: thousands of candidate statements; precision is high because 勧請 prose almost always names a real source shrine. Ambiguity (multiple kanjō over history) survives as multiple cited statements.
  • Effort: small — one generator in the existing reisai/bunrei pattern; the parser is a regex, not NLP.

2. NDL Digital Collections — pre-war 神社明細帳 & 府県神社誌 authoritativeOCR effort

The National Diet Library has digitized large numbers of pre-war shrine registries (神社明細帳, 府県郡誌の神社誌, 神社大観 etc.), public domain and free online — these are the ancestors of the 1995 神社本庁 survey the paper route wanted. Per-shrine entries record 祭神, 由緒, and 勧請 provenance.

  • Method: NDL Digital Collections API (iss.ndl.go.jp/api / dl.ndl.go.jp) full-text search for 勧請 within digitized shrine registries; NDL's own OCR text layer is searchable for many volumes — no OCR work of ours needed for those.
  • Yield: authoritative period documentation; citable (S248 the digitized volume + S304 page). Best used to verify and deepen networks rather than mass-import.
  • Effort: medium — API harvest is easy; deciding how to model 1900-era data against present shrines is the real work.

3. Prefectural 神社庁 databases medium yield47 scrapers

Most of the 47 prefectural jinjachō publish per-shrine pages (e.g. Tokyo, Hyōgo, Fukuoka, Saitama) with 由緒 text and 祭神 — many state 勧請 provenance. Coverage is official (神社本庁-affiliated shrines, ~78k) and per-shrine.

  • Method: per-prefecture scrapers (formats differ wildly — this is the cost). Same 勧請 regex as avenue 1.
  • Yield: covers small shrines jawiki never will; official provenance.
  • Effort: large in aggregate; best done opportunistically, top prefectures first.

4. onkamui Rakuten blog queued — Emma approved the maximalist parser

~50 networks with named branch enumerations in hierarchical prose. Already decided on the wiki [[Open questions]] page: attempt a well-scoped maximalist parser → middle path (named networks only) → easy path → give up. Sits in queue.md.

5. Official 総本社 branch registries per-network

Several head shrines publish their own branch lists: Fushimi Inari's 講務本庁 network, Kotohira-gū's 崇敬会 lists, Hachimangū Rengō (八幡宮連合), Suwa-taisha's 全国諏訪神社 materials. Highest possible authority for their own network; one small scraper each. Good for networks where jinja-kikou coverage looks thin.

6. 宗教年鑑 (Agency for Cultural Affairs, annual, free PDF) counts only

Authoritative counts per religious corporation/lineage, no per-shrine rows. Replaces exactly the "authoritative 系統 counts" role the 1995 survey would have played — useful as a validation yardstick (is our Hachiman network plausibly ~10k?) rather than as an edge source.

7. Japan Search LOD / community shrine databases low marginal yield

Japan Search (jpsearch.go.jp) SPARQL federates GLAM datasets — worth one exploratory query session, but the 4-agent sweep suggests shrine lineage isn't in it. Community sites (yaokami.jp, jinjajin.jp, omairi.club, goshuin databases) have per-shrine 由緒 text — same harvest as avenue 3 with murkier citability.

Recommendation

Do avenue 1 (jawiki 勧請 prose harvest) first. It is one generator on infrastructure we already run, its citations are the same S4656 jawiki-URL pattern as the reisai import, and it upgrades the whole dataset from "network head by suffix" to "actual named kanjō parent" wherever prose exists. Avenue 2 (NDL) is the true paper-replacement for authority; avenue 4 (onkamui) is already queued. Avenues 3/5 are opportunistic follow-ups; 6 is a sanity yardstick; 7 is an afternoon of curiosity at most.
